name: Pixel Value Differencing
description: Detects stego-like pixel value differencing patterns that leak into AI-generated images (Wu & Tsai, 2003).
mechanism:
This method applies Pixel Value Differencing (PVD) analysis following Wu & Tsai (2003) for steganographic and manipulation detection:

1. **Block Partitioning**: The image is divided into non-overlapping blocks of two consecutive pixels. For each block, the difference value dₖ = |pᵢ − pᵢ₊₁| is computed between adjacent pixel pairs in both horizontal and vertical directions.

2. **Difference Histogram Construction**: A histogram of all pixel difference values is constructed. Natural images exhibit a characteristic PVD histogram following a Laplacian-like distribution — high concentration near zero (smooth regions) with exponential decay toward larger differences (edge regions).

3. **Range Table Analysis**: Differences are classified into ranges [lₖ, uₖ] following the PVD range table. Each range has an expected capacity proportional to its width. Steganographic embedding modifies the histogram within these ranges in detectable ways — creating artifacts in the distribution tails.

4. **Statistical Regularity Detection**: The method detects statistical anomalies in the PVD histogram: (a) unnatural steps between adjacent bins caused by embedding algorithms, (b) abnormal symmetry or flatness in typically peaked distributions, (c) deviations from the expected Benford-like first-digit distribution of differences.

5. **AI Generation Indicators**: AI-generated images typically exhibit PVD histograms with abnormal smoothness (lacking the fine-grained irregularities of real camera quantization), unusual uniformity across difference ranges, or artificial periodicity absent in natural pixel statistics. The analysis score quantifies these deviations.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models

references.title: Wu, D.C. & Tsai, W.H. (2003). A Steganographic Method for Images by Pixel-Value Differencing. Pattern Recognition Letters.
